ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human safety reviewer with the trip telemetry (speed, harsh braking/acceleration, shoulder use) for the 21:22–21:34 window; reviewer to contact the rider via RydeHELP, note the 995 / driver commercial-insurance path, and confirm no automatic fare action while the fixed RydeX fare stands.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety-type dispute: the rider alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking on a RydeX trip, and that they felt unsafe [F1][F2][F6]. Per SAFE-1 the safety screen is mandatory for every case and per SAFE-2 any allegation of dangerous driving removes the case from automatic adjudication [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The trace marks SAFE-1 ✓ and the only permitted outcome as escalate, so I do not decide the fare or any refund.

The ride record itself is neutral and cannot dispose of the allegation: the route was not a deviation (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal, -0.1 km) and the trip was slightly quicker than estimate (12.7 min vs 13.8 min), which is consistent with either normal driving or the rider's account of aggressive driving [F1][F2]. Speeding, harsh braking and shoulder use are not visible in these measures [F1][F2], and the fare was a fixed quote for RydeX, so nothing here turns on RD-2 or FARE-1 [FARE-1].

The only driving-related statements in the record are the rider's complaint and the driver's denial, which was written after the trip: "I drove normally. The rider was on the phone the whole trip and never complained to me." [F6]. That is a post-hoc claim, not a record of the driving, and it does not settle whether the alleged driving occurred; a driver's later statement cannot override the need for human review of a dangerous-driving allegation [F6][SAFE-1]. The chat is short and complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and contains only pickup logistics — rider at the MRT taxi stand, driver 4 minutes away in a blue Prius — with no threats, insults or abusive language from either party [F3][F4][F5]. I therefore read the message set (and the driver's statement) for SAFE-1 indicators and find none of threat, intimidation, harassment or sexual remark; what remains is the driving-conduct allegation, which is a SAFE-2 matter [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-2]. Profiles are neutral and cannot decide the case: rider 4.6, no prior disputes; driver 4.85 with 963 trips and no upheld disputes, so RD-6's repeated-violation condition is not met and no account flag follows from it [F7][F8][RD-6].

For the human reviewer: what happened — rider reports speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking on the 21:22–21:34 Jurong East MRT → NUS trip, charged $20.85 fixed; what is disputed — whether the driving was dangerous, which the trip metrics cannot resolve; what to check — the telemetry (speed, harsh-braking/acceleration events, shoulder usage) for the trip window, and the rider's and driver's accounts [F1][F2][F6]. Rider-facing paths: RydeHELP report, and 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance if medical attention is needed [SAFE-2]. The record does not let me decide the driving allegation, so evidence_status is insufficient and the case escalates rather than ruling on the fare [SAFE-2].
